This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 15.11.2023 at about 9.45 p.m. petitioner was riding TVS XL bearing Reg. No.KA-50-H-2517 near Bramhadevarahalli Village, Nagamangala - Mysore Road, SCCH-5 Hosakere Hobli, he has stopped his TVS XL to take right turn for crossing, at that time, a Maruthi Suzuki Alto Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-N-7549 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the TVS XL Moped and caused accident and due to this accident, petitioner sustained injuries and his TVS XL was also badly damaged.
Soon after the accident, petitioner was shifted to AC Giri Hospital, Bellur Cross and took treatment as inpatient and spent more than Rs.1,50,000/-towards treatment and medical expenses.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 75 years, doing agriculture work and earning Rs.3,00,000/- per anum and Rs.25,000/- from coconut buying.
Due to the accident, he is suffering from mental and physical deformity.

With regard to accident crime No.160/2023 is registered against the driver of the SCCH-5 offending Maruthi Suzuki 800 Alto Car before the Nagamangala Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared before court and filed written statement.

Further submitted that, alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Suzuki Alto 800 Car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-7549 and also submitted that, said vehicle has been insured with respondent No.2 with policy No.13532454 valid from 30.07.2023 to 29.07.2024 and respondent No.1 has a SCCH-5 valid driving licence.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further submitted that, respondent No.2 is insurer of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-N-7549 and liability to indemnify respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.2 seeks protection under Sec.147 and 150(2) of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, there is no negligence on the part of driver of the said car and driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further denied age,
occupation and SCCH-5 income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:

::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 15.11.2023 at about 9.45 p.m. due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Suzuki Alto Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 50-N-7549?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, Petitioner himself examined as PW-1, examined Dr.Mahesh D.V.,
Professor and HOD at Adichunchanagiri Institute of Medical Sciences as PW-2 and marked 16 documents as per SCCH-5 Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative
Issue No.3 :

As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined himself as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
In order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of SCCH-5 complaint as Ex.P.2,
copy of crime detail report as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.7.
10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, petitioner has examined Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 15.11.2023 as alleged in the petition.

11. Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to discard the evidence of PW-1.

In the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 15.11.2023 at about 9.45 p.m. SCCH-5 when he was riding TVS XL bearing Reg. No.KA-50-H- 2517 near Bramhadevarahalli Village,
Shivalingaiah vs Muniyappa S M on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130157083/
3 Nagamangala - Mysore Road, Hosakere Hobli.
12.
It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Maruthi Suzuki Alto Car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-N-7549.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained tenderness over the left shoulder joint, movements are restricted, tenderness over the left shoulder joint, left thigh, left parietal region, left foot, right ankle and abrasion injury, non-united fracture of the humerus of left side with implant failure and SCCH-5 comminuted lateral and clavicle fracture.

For the said injuries,
he was operated with open reduction and internal fixation with locking compression plage and G bone graft for humerus and K wiring for lateral end clavicle fracture.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Adichunchanagiri Hospital & Research Centre, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 15.11.2023 to 29.11.2023.

Further he has exhibited medical prescriptions as Ex.P.11 and medial bills of Rs.37,452/-.
14.

Further Dr.Mahesh D.V. Professor and HOD at Adichunchanagiri Institute of Medical Sciences,
Bellur is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited case sheet as Ex.P.13,
OPD record as Ex.P.14, calculation sheet as Ex.P.15 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.16.
SCCH-5
Further PW-2 has assessed physical disability of 40% of left upper limb and 13.87% for whole body.
In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, at the time of discharge of petitioner his condition was stable and requires further treatment for correction of non union of humerus.
Further deposed that, usually age old patient has arthritis problem and for exclusive clavicle fracture, the disability is assessed around 8-10% for whole body.
Further deposed that he has assessed only physical disability and elbow and wrist movements are normal.
Further deposed that, except shoulder muscle power, the muscle power is normal.
Further deposed that, the petitioner is right handed.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner the functional disability of the SCCH-5 petitioner is considered at the rate of 11%, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 75 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.8, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1943 and the alleged accident is occurred on 15.11.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.8 his age is considered about 81 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 2 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

hence said multiplier is taken into consideration.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10, petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 14 days.

As per the evidence of PW-2 he examined petitioner on 28.08.2025 i.e., after 9 months and on examination date as per version of PW-2 and by considering the gravity of injury sustained by petitioner it may take at least three months to heal the wound.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.48,000/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss on income during laid up period.

. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.37,452/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 15.11.2023.
So as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained fracture of shaft of eft clavicle, fracture of distal end of proximal phalynx which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Muniyappa S.N. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5 19.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,82,692/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

21. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.13532454 which is valid for the period from SCCH-5 30.07.2023 to 29.07.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.11.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that,
respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: :
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,82,692- (Rupees one lakh eighty two thousand six hundred and ninety two Only) SCCH-5 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof .
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
